findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/MvPolynomial/Eval.lean:590 `theorem aeval_X (s : σ) : aeval f (X s) = f s`; :604 `theorem aeval_X_left : aeval X = AlgHom.id`; :684 `aeval_monomial`; Mathlib/Algebra/MvPolynomial/Eval.lean:114 `eval₂_X_pow : ((X s) ^ n).eval₂ f g = (g s) ^ n`; Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/AlgebraMap.lean:303 `aeval_X_pow : aeval x ((X : R[X]) ^ n) = x ^ n`.
findings.fix: Give the curve a name and name the lemmas after it: e.g. `def monomialCurve (a : σ → R) (c : σ → ℕ) : σ → Polynomial R := fun i ↦ Polynomial.C (a i) + Polynomial.X ^ c i`, then `aeval_monomialCurve`, `coeff_aeval_monomialCurve`, `aeval_monomialCurve_ne_zero`, `natTrailingDegree_aeval_monomialCurve`, `trailingCoeff_aeval_monomialCurve`; likewise `aeval_monomial_X_pow_left` (or `aeval_X_pow_left_monomial`) for line 178. Failing that, mark the family position with `_left` per `aeval_X_left`.
findings.issue: Inside `namespace MvPolynomial`, `aeval_C_add_X_pow` and friends name the substituted family `fun i ↦ Polynomial.C (a i) + Polynomial.X ^ c i`, but Mathlib's convention is that the suffix after `aeval` names the polynomial argument (`MvPolynomial.aeval_X`, `aeval_C`, `aeval_monomial`, `Polynomial.aeval_X_pow`, `MvPolynomial.eval₂_X_pow`), with `aeval_X_left` the device for naming the family. Worse, in this namespace `C`/`X` read as `MvPolynomial.C`/`MvPolynomial.X`, so the names advertise lemmas about the argument `C r + X i ^ n` rather than about substituting a `Polynomial R`-valued curve. Same defect at lines 178 (`aeval_X_pow_monomial`), 199 (`coeff_aeval_C_add_X_pow`), 379, 393, 406, 416 (also cited in the module docstring, line 60), 429.

findings.evidence: Line 381 conclusion `(aeval … p).coeff k = 0`; line 231 `coeff_taylor_eq_zero_of_lt_lazardValuation`; Mathlib precedent `MvPowerSeries.coeff_eq_zero_of_lt_lexOrder` (mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/LexOrder.lean:83).
findings.fix: Rename to `coeff_aeval_C_add_X_pow_eq_zero_of_lt_weight` (or `coeff_aeval_monomialCurve_eq_zero_of_lt_weight` under the rename above).
findings.issue: `coeff_aeval_C_add_X_pow_of_lt` proves `coeff k = 0` but omits `eq_zero`, so it reads as a hypothesis-constrained variant of the computation lemma `coeff_aeval_C_add_X_pow` (line 199) rather than a vanishing statement; the `_of_lt` also does not say what `k` is below. The file's own sibling `coeff_taylor_eq_zero_of_lt_lazardValuation` (line 231) spells it out.

summary: Names in the `lazardValuation`/evaluator API are sound and track the adjacent `orderAt` file, but the eight `aeval_C_add_X_pow` / `aeval_X_pow_monomial` names invert Mathlib's `aeval_*` convention (the suffix names the argument, not the substituted family) and read as `MvPolynomial.C`/`X` when the lemmas are about `Polynomial.C`/`X`; one name also hides an `= 0` conclusion.
